questions.q: What is the fundamental unit of I/O in SQL Server?
options: The 8 KB page
The 64 KB extent
The row
The data file
questions.explain: SQL Server always reads and writes whole 8 KB pages, never partial ones.

questions.q: What's the difference between a uniform extent and a mixed extent?
options: A uniform extent's eight pages all belong to one object; a mixed extent's eight pages can belong to several objects
A uniform extent is for indexes only; a mixed extent is for tables only
A uniform extent is 8 KB; a mixed extent is 64 KB
There is no difference — the terms are interchangeable
questions.explain: Small new objects start in mixed extents to avoid wasting space; once an object grows, SQL Server allocates uniform extents to it.

questions.q: Why is a physical read more expensive than a logical read?
options: A logical read is served from the buffer pool in memory; a physical read has to come from disk
A physical read is served from memory; a logical read has to come from disk
Physical reads only happen during backups
There is no performance difference between them
questions.explain: Logical reads hit already-cached pages in the buffer pool; physical reads mean the page wasn't cached and had to be pulled from disk, which is far slower.

questions.q: What does the checkpoint process do?
options: Writes current dirty pages from the buffer pool to disk, shortening crash recovery time
Frees buffer pool memory by evicting unused pages
Rebuilds indexes
Resizes the transaction log
questions.explain: Checkpoint makes the data files consistent with the buffer pool so less transaction log needs replaying after a crash — it doesn't by itself free memory.

questions.q: What does the lazy writer do that checkpoint does not?
options: It evicts pages that haven't been used recently, freeing buffer pool memory for pages the workload needs now
It writes the transaction log to disk
It compiles execution plans
It runs only when the service is shut down
questions.explain: Lazy writer specifically manages buffer pool memory pressure, flushing and evicting cold pages so the cache stays useful — separate from checkpoint's job of shortening recovery.
